Shine it on what turns and change the rate until it seems to stand still: at that rate, it turns once a flash. A phone\'s torch switches slowly, so the rate is capped at %1$s Hz (%2$s RPM), and many torches stop keeping up sooner (the rate reached is shown while it flashes). For something faster, a flash every second or third turn freezes it too: its speed is then a whole multiple of the rate, found with ×2.
Flashing light can trigger seizures in people with photosensitive epilepsy.
